system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status:** Internal advice – positions below are against the Buyer Playbook. Seller statements such as "agreed", "settled", "addressed" or "considered adequate" are the Seller's characterisations only and have not been confirmed through our authority process.

**Headline:** The Seller Update is materially worse than our playbook on every liability-regime point, and – importantly – the Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts several of the reassuring statements in the Seller Update (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses). We should reject the package as a whole and respond with a full mark-up. No fallback has been authorised by Amelia Frost on any item.

---

| Ref | Issue | Seller position | Buyer should want | Recommendation (one-line reason) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001** | General liability cap | 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (cl 12.1). | 25% / AUD 6,000,000. | **Reject; hold 25%.** 20% is our conditional fallback, but it is not "cleared" merely because the Seller's number matches it – no written Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft exists. |
| **SPA-N-002** | De minimis & basket | De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; excess-only (deductible) recovery (cl 12.2). | De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; tipping basket (first-dollar recovery once exceeded). | **Reject; counter at playbook figures.** Seller's thresholds are 5x ours and the deductible structure permanently strands AUD 250,000 of loss. |
| **SPA-N-003** | General claims time limit | 18 months (cl 12.3/13), plus a default that any limitation applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | 24 months; limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims expressly. | **Reject; hold 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost written approval (none given), and the default-override language is a hidden general-regime override (see SPA-N-014). |
| **SPA-N-004** | Fundamental/Title regime | Capacity and title warranties subject to same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity". | Separate regime: 100% of price cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar. | **Reject outright.** Title to the shares is the entire bargain; collapsing it into a 20%/18-month regime is not simplification, it is a transfer of fundamental risk to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-005** | Fraud carve-out | None offered; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature". | Express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; non-waivable. | **Non-negotiable; insert express carve-out.** The Seller's "all Claims of any nature" wording would purport to cap and time-bar fraud – unacceptable and must be corrected before any other liability point is traded. |
| **SPA-N-006** | Disclosure scope | General disclosure of entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012 as at 22 Sept 2026), Accounts, statutory registers and public records (Sch 7; DL 1.1–1.2). | Specific fair disclosure only, with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. | **Reject general disclosure; require fair-disclosure standard.** Whole-data-room disclosure plus the cl 8.3 knowledge bar would effectively nullify the warranty package. |
| **SPA-N-007** | Buyer knowledge qualifier | Blanket exclusion for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3). | Delete the blanket exclusion. Any knowledge qualifier must be on the Seller side – named seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry – and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Delete cl 8.3.** A "discoverable" standard is constructive knowledge and, combined with SPA-N-006, shifts the entire DD burden onto the Buyer; it must not apply to title, capacity, fraud or indemnities. |
| **SPA-N-008** | Bluefen consent (~AUD 3.6m / ~30% FY26 revenue) | "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition deemed satisfied on delivery of written consent (cl 3/6.3). DL §2 confirms **no final written consent and no evidence conditions under cl 11.3 are satisfied**. | Condition precedent requiring (a) effective consent and (b) evidence that all cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion. | **Reject.** The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts "addressed"; reasonable endeavours is insufficient for a 30%-revenue customer and consent-on-delivery ignores the cl 11.3 conditions. |
| **SPA-N-009** | Riverlark facility (~AUD 3.2m) | Release "to be provided following Completion" (cl 2/7). DL §3 confirms facility **not repaid** and no final discharge of security. | Current payout figure; direct repayment from Completion funds; effective security releases delivered at Completion. Post-completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval. | **Reject; require payout and release at Completion.** We would otherwise acquire an encumbered company with a change-of-control trigger (cl 8.1) live; no Amelia Frost approval exists for a post-completion structure. |
| **SPA-N-010** | Employee bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000) | "A matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. DL §5 confirms **not in the draft funds flow** and silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs. | Specific line item in funds flow (or seller-funded with escrow/price adjustment) covering AUD 420,000 **plus** triggered on-costs; quantify on-costs. | **Reject; insist on express line item.** "A matter for the Seller" is not a mechanism, and silent exclusion from the funds flow means the Company (i.e. the Buyer) bears the cost post-Completion. Also note the "agreed price mechanics" statement is not accepted. |
| **SPA-N-011** | Ironquay IP indemnity | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" (cl 11.1). DL §4: cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but not independently verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room. | Broadened indemnity covering loss arising from any defect in title to or transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials, preserving the SOW3 cure; independent verification of the AUD 180,000 status. | **Broaden the indemnity; do not accept "adequate".** The underlying IP may not have transferred at all; a payment-only indemnity does not cover loss of use, re-development or third-party claims. |
| **SPA-N-012** | Export/privacy incident (DD-006, ~1,240 records) | "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" (cl 4.6/Sch 6). DL §6: unknown whether accessed, exact scope or whether notification required; investigation preliminary. | Preserve logs; complete investigation; pre-Completion written updates; specific warranty/indemnity for notification, remediation and regulatory cost if a breach is later confirmed. | **Do not accept materiality assertion; require covenant to investigate and update.** Per playbook, assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction – but "not expected to be material" is the Seller's unsupported conclusion. |
| **SPA-N-013** | Sandbar renewals (3 x AUD 110,000 = AUD 330,000) | "Ordinary-course operating costs". DL §8: silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Assessment of timing, terminability and accrual status (DD-008 and DD-011 read together); classification only after assessment. | **Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction, but do not accept "ordinary course" as settled.** The Seller's label and its own disclosure are inconsistent – obtain the facts before classifying. |
| **SPA-N-014** | Category separation | "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature". | Title, Tax, IP, payment obligations and covenants each in separate regimes; general limitations apply only where expressly stated. | **Delete the default-override language.** It is a hidden general-regime override that would quietly import the 20%/18-month cap into Title, Tax, IP, indemnities and covenants. |
| **SPA-N-015** | Title verification | Title "evidenced by" the share register at DD-012. DL §10 concedes this is merely the source relied on and that Buyer has not completed its own verification. | Independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence: ASIC searches, PPSR, constitution, board/shareholder authorisations, and Riverlark release (security likely over shares/assets). | **Do not accept DD-012 as proof.** It is a Seller-supplied internal register; independent verification is required, particularly with a live Riverlark security. |
| **SPA-N-016** | Tax / IP open terms | "Settled under the general regime above". | Terms remain OPEN; separate Tax and IP regimes to be negotiated; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. | **Reject "settled".** Nothing has been agreed through our authority process; folding Tax and IP into a 20%/18-month general regime would be a significant concession made by default. |

---

## Cross-cutting observations

1. **Disclosure Letter vs Seller Update – use the inconsistency.** The Seller Update says Bluefen is "addressed", Riverlark is "addressed", and funds flow is "agreed"; the Disclosure Letter (§§2, 3, 5) confirms none of those things is true as at 22 September 2026. Our response should cite the Seller's own disclosures back to them.

2. **No fallbacks are authorised.** The 20% cap and 18-month period match our conditional fallbacks, but no written Amelia Frost authority identifying this draft has been given. Per playbook §0.4/6.3, a match of numbers is not clearance. Hold starting positions.

3. **The liability package operates cumulatively.** General disclosure (N-006) + constructive buyer knowledge (N-007) + deductible basket (N-002) + all-Claims override (N-003/N-014) + no fraud carve-out (N-005) would together leave the Buyer with little practical recourse. These should be rejected together, not traded individually.

4. **Facts to refresh before the next turn:** independent title/encumbrance searches; Riverlark current payout; Bluefen cl 11.3 condition status; Ironquay payment status (bank-verified); DD-006 investigation progress; Sandbar renewal terms; on-cost quantum for DD-005.

5. **Reservation (DL §11) cuts both ways.** The Seller expressly states no negotiation position or approval is included in the Disclosure Letter – so nothing in it can be treated as a concession by us either.
=== END ADVICE ===
